title: By the mount where Allah spoke to Musa.
subtitle: Why a mountain opens the surah
then: The tafsir says Allah swears by His creation {idea}as a testimony to His great ability.{/idea} At-Tur is a mount with trees, like the one {reward}where Allah spoke to Musa.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ was heard reciting this surah in Maghrib, and a listener said he never heard a more beautiful recitation.
now: You have a place that changed you: the masjid where you first cried in prayer, a hospital chapel, a quiet beach at dawn. {idea}Places can testify.{/idea} This surah starts at one of the greatest of them.
old: A mountain is just part of the scenery.
new: Some places carry the memory of Allah speaking, and they call me to listen.
try: Go back, in person or in memory, to one place where you felt close to Allah, and sit there for five minutes.

title: By a Book that is already written.
subtitle: The inscribed Book
then: Allah swears by {idea}a Book inscribed.{/idea} The tafsir gives two views: the Preserved Tablet, or {idea}the revealed Books that people recite.{/idea} Either way, what is written with Allah does not change.
now: You write a to-do list and lose it by Tuesday. Contracts get rewritten, promises get broken. {idea}This Book does not get rewritten.{/idea} What Allah promises in it is as firm as ink that never fades.
old: Promises are words that can change.
new: Allah's word is written and fixed. His promise is the most certain thing there is.
try: Open the Quran today and read one page slowly, as words that will not change.

title: Written on open parchment, spread out to be read.
subtitle: A Book meant to be opened
then: The Book is {reward}in parchment unrolled.{/reward} The tafsir links this to the revealed Books {idea}that people recite.{/idea} It is not a sealed secret but something laid open.
now: There is a Quran in your house, maybe wrapped in cloth on the top shelf, opened in Ramadan and at funerals. {reward}It was sent spread open.{/reward} It is meant for your Tuesday evenings too.
old: The Quran is precious, so I keep it safely closed.
new: Its honor is in being opened and read, not only kept.
try: Take the Quran off the shelf and leave it somewhere you will see it tomorrow.

title: By the House in heaven always full of worshippers.
subtitle: Al-Bayt Al-Ma'mur
then: The Prophet ﷺ said that on the Night Journey he was taken to {idea}Al-Bayt Al-Ma'mur{/idea}, visited daily by seventy thousand angels who never return to it again. He saw Ibrahim reclining against it. The tafsir notes {reward}Ibrahim built the Ka'bah on earth, and the reward fits the action.{/reward}
now: You feel like you are praying alone in a small room. Right now, angels without number are circling a House in heaven. {idea}Your prayer joins a worship that never stops.{/idea}
old: My worship is small and lonely.
new: My prayer joins a worship in heaven that never pauses.
try: In your next prayer, remember for a moment that the angels are worshipping with you.

title: By the roof raised high above you.
subtitle: The sky as a guarded ceiling
then: Ali bin Abi Talib said the raised roof {idea}means the heaven{/idea}, and recited: We made the heaven a roof, {reward}safe and well-guarded{/reward}, {trap}yet they turn away from its signs.{/trap}
now: You notice the ceiling only when it leaks. The sky over your city has never leaked, never cracked, never fallen. {idea}A guarded roof you never pay for.{/idea} Most days you never even look at it.
old: I only notice the roof over me when something goes wrong.
new: The sky is a roof Allah keeps guarded for me every second.
try: Look up at the sky once today and thank Allah for the roof you never had to fix.

title: By the sea that is full, and will one day blaze.
subtitle: The calm sea and what it will become

row.title: the sea will always be calm

then: Most scholars say this is {idea}the oceans of the earth.{/idea} One view in the tafsir: on the Day of Resurrection {trap}the sea will be kindled with fire{/trap}, as in another verse. Qatadah and Ibn Jarir preferred {idea}the filled sea{/idea}, since it is not lit now.
now: You stand on a beach, the waves steady, the horizon endless. It feels like it will always be this way. {idea}Nothing in creation is fixed except by Allah's will.{/idea} The world you think is permanent has a last day.
old: The world around me is solid and will stay the same.
new: Even the oceans are held in place by Allah, and one day they will change.
try: Next time you see water, a sea, a river, or a glass, remember for a moment that it obeys Allah.

title: Everything sworn by points to this: it will happen.
subtitle: The answer to the oaths

row.title: a true vow
sub: it stopped him in the street

then: After five oaths comes the point: {trap}the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass.{/trap} The tafsir reports that Umar once heard a man reciting this at night in Madinah and said, {idea}by the Lord of the Ka'bah, this is a true vow.{/idea} He went home and was ill for a month.
now: You have heard this verse in Taraweeh, maybe a dozen times, and it slid past. Umar heard it once through a wall and sat down in the street. {idea}Let one verse actually land on you.{/idea}
old: I know these verses already. They are familiar.
new: Familiar words can still be true vows that should stop me.
try: Read this one verse slowly three times today, and sit with it for a minute.

title: When it comes, nothing can push it back.
subtitle: No preventer
then: The tafsir says that {trap}when Allah decides to send the torment, none can prevent it or stop it.{/trap} The Makkans had wealth, tribes, and alliances. None of that would be a shield. {idea}This is the part of the vow that shook Umar.{/idea}
now: You have a lawyer for a contract, insurance for the car, a friend who knows someone. You can push almost anything back a little. {idea}This one, no one can.{/idea} {reward}But today the door to turn back is wide open.{/reward}
old: There is always someone who can get me out of trouble.
new: Some things no one can stop, so the time to prepare is now.
try: Make sincere istighfar for something specific, while the door is still open.

title: The sky that held still will shake and spin.
subtitle: The raised roof, on that Day
then: Verse 5 swore by the roof raised high. Now that same sky {trap}will sway with circular motion.{/trap} The tafsir gives the meanings: shaking violently, splitting, spinning. {idea}The word holds both shaking and spinning.{/idea}
now: An earthquake alert buzzes on your phone and for three seconds everything you trusted feels unsteady. {idea}That feeling is a tiny preview.{/idea} The only firm ground is what you built with Allah.
old: The world under and above me is stable.
new: Only Allah is truly stable. Even the sky will move when He commands.
try: Say one dua today asking Allah to make you steady on the Day when everything shakes.

title: The mountains will move off like dust.
subtitle: What seems fixed forever
then: The surah opened with a mountain. Now {trap}the mountains will pass on, departing.{/trap} The tafsir says they will fade away and become {trap}scattered particles of dust blown away by the wind.{/trap}
now: You say solid as a rock about your job, your health, your plans. The rocks themselves will blow away like dust. {idea}Anchor yourself to what does not move.{/idea}
old: Some things in my life are rock solid.
new: Even mountains will become dust. Only what is with Allah stays.
try: Name one thing you call permanent. Then do one small deed that will truly last.

title: That Day will be heavy for those who denied it.
subtitle: Woe to the deniers

row.title: the deniers
sub: who said it would not come

then: With the sky shaking and mountains gone, the verse turns to people: {trap}woe that Day to those who denied.{/trap} The tafsir says the woe is the punishment Allah directs at them. The surah introduction notes that the Makkans called the Prophet ﷺ a sorcerer and a madman.
now: You do not deny the Day out loud. But some weeks you live as if it is not coming: no prayer, no thought of it. {idea}Denial can be quiet.{/idea} It shows in how you spend your days.
old: I believe in the Day, so this does not apply to me.
new: Belief shows in how I live, not only in what I say.
try: Look at yesterday honestly. Find one moment where you lived as if the Day was not real, and change it today.

title: They spent their days in empty talk and play.
subtitle: Who the deniers were
then: The deniers are described: {trap}those who were, in their falsehood, playing.{/trap} The tafsir says they live in falsehood and {trap}make the religion the subject of their mockery and jest.{/trap}
now: Hours in a group chat trading memes about religion. A comedy show where faith is always the punchline. You laugh along. {idea}Play is fine. Making the sacred a joke is not.{/idea}
new: What I keep laughing at slowly becomes what I cannot take seriously.
try: Next time a joke about faith comes up, simply do not add to it.
